subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` knob now, and must this PR preserve shipped no-override `bootstrap-extra-files` behavior for subagent and cron sessions?
rationale: The implementation gap is clear, but the choice changes public config semantics and existing session context for documented hook setups, which automation should not decide.

options.title: Preserve shipped defaults, then review tiering
options.body: Keep no-override `bootstrap-extra-files` behavior unchanged, apply hook-source exclusion only to explicit tier modes, add docs/tests, then continue maintainer review of the additive config surface.

options.title: Accept the root-only default break
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally make subagent and cron defaults root-only, but the PR should include explicit upgrade notes and compatibility proof for affected hook users.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap selection
options.body: Pause this PR and resolve tiering with broader context/bootstrap selection proposals so OpenClaw gets one long-term public contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve shipped defaults, then review tiering
recommendation.body: Keep no-override `bootstrap-extra-files` behavior unchanged, apply hook-source exclusion only to explicit tier modes, add docs/tests, then continue maintainer review of the additive config surface.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest feature-history signal for subagent bootstrap limiting and prior maintainer-side review context on the paired issue.
